content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history.
- Model shows persistent lag in recognizing downward trends; true outcomes often dip faster than forecasted.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to smoothly decay toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually adjust — but often too late to catch sharp reversals.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices; fails to anticipate sharp rebounds from troughs.
- High volatility in history is not fully captured — model smooths out extremes, leading to underestimation of volatility-driven price swings.
- Forecasts are more accurate in the final 10–15 days of the 30-day window, suggesting model improves with time but still lags on initial spikes.
